decisions.text: type arrow: two periods: the change between them is the point (06 DP6-3, G1.46): the default is an arrow chart, each category's change in units and in % side by side (G1.47), or a chart of the change itself (the % panel alone, facts.message relative_change; or the change as bars, a previous_period comparison with transform deviation); clustered bars of the two periods only where each period's own values, not the change, are what the request needs: facts.message periods, with the reason, grounded in the request, in reasons["facts.message"]
the values are not far from zero compared with their spread
two panels sharing the rows: the values, before to after; the change in %, from 0 % (G1.47, G7.21)
rows by the before value, largest first; last: Lowther Park (a value not known)
arrows in the good colour where the change is good and the bad colour where it is bad (higher is better; G7.22, D-40)
the % panel: −50–20 by 10, holding 0 %, where its arrows start
the % panel's labels would crowd in its width: −60–20 by 20
the values in the measure's unit, 0–400,000 by 100,000, each arrow from before to after; the scale's title below: “Loans (thousands of physical items issued)”
the change in %, −60–20 by 20, each arrow from 0 %; the scale's title below: “Change in loans”
an arrow chart (G7.21): a dot at the start, a shaft, a head whose tip sits exactly on the end value; one row per category, its name at the left

changes shorter than a full head with its start dot, their direction kept readable (--arrow-short-head: fit): the head over the start dot, haloed: Northfield (values), St Mary's (values), Oakham (values), Westbrook (values); the head shrunk to fit between the start dot and the end: Riverside (values)
the key “2019” and “2025” over the two ends of Central's arrow, no legend (G7.21)
the title wraps onto two lines

static output, in colour: one file, red for bad and green for good, plain, for every reader (D-18; owner, 1 Oct 2026); black and white (audience.bw_risk) adds the textures, and a style may choose the colour-blind-safe pair (--good-bad-mode: safe-pair)
notes under the chart, below everything else, left-aligned and wrapped to its 440 pt: 1 plain note (marks in reading order)

findings.message: two periods (2019, 2025) with facts.message periods but no reason: the change between two periods is the point unless the request says otherwise, so the route stays the arrow chart; the default is an arrow chart, each category's change in units and in % side by side (G1.47), or a chart of the change itself (the % panel alone, facts.message relative_change; or the change as bars, a previous_period comparison with transform deviation); clustered bars of the two periods only where each period's own values, not the change, are what the request needs: facts.message periods, with the reason, grounded in the request, in reasons["facts.message"]
findings.title: two periods: an arrow chart

findings.message: the values are read as good or bad, with no comparison value or dividing value: a target, budget or average would say how to feel about them (G8.12, G0.19)
findings.title: comparison values where the audience lacks context: targets and budgets before averages, previous periods and peers

findings.message: highlighting an arrow is a later stage
findings.title: requested but not drawn in this stage of the generator

findings.message: the note “opened Sept. 2021” of the value of lowther-park at 2019: nothing in the chart writes that value (a gap in a line has no text to mark), so the note stands under the chart without a mark
findings.title: notes under the chart: every mark with its note and every footnote with its mark, the notes below everything else, wrapped to the chart's width, never clipped or dropped (owner, 1 Oct 2026)
